newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM vows to improve ties with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM vows to improve ties with Russia.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto vowed on Thursday to drastically improve long-strained relations with Russia.
"We must improve overall bilateral relations with Russia to the level where the two countries can enjoy their own national interests," Hashimoto told business leaders.

A bitter row over a group of small islands, called the Southern Kuriles by Russia and Northern Territories by Japan, has overshadowed the bilateral ties and blocked the signing of a formal peace treaty ending World War Two hostilities.
"When it comes to resolving the issue of the Northern Territories, no one should be a loser," Hashimoto said. "But I would like to tell you that it is not that easy."
In 1993 during Russian President Boris Yeltsin's visit to Tokyo, Russia agreed in a joint communiqu that the dispute itself existed and should be resolved by "law and justice".
Hashimoto said he wanted to hold a summit with Yeltsin later this year. The two leaders met last month in Denver on the sidelines of the G7 Summit.
"I am hoping to meet President Yeltsin again and deepen mutual trust and friendship," Hashimoto said.
He added he would propose that the two countries jointly explore energy resources in Siberia and Russian Far East.

"Russia is a country endowed with massive natural resources," Hashimoto said. "Efficient use of the resources would contribute not only to the development of the Russian economy, but also to the stability of the world energy market."
